items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: His name, his records sound familiar, you know?

ctx.x: Well I managed to mix up the real baddest fellas, you know, playing piano. That's why I learned to develop so well, because I learned so many different actions and changes and cross-cord by listening to one through the other. I said well I take them all and put them in the sack together so I play a little bit of all of their music, plus what I can think of myself. And that's how I learned how to play piano.

What do you think, you know Otis Spann? You ever heard him? He's Muddy Waters, our piano player. No, he wasn't from here. No, no. He's up around Chicago. No, I don't know. I don't think he played in New Orleans really. But I thought you might have known him somehow. Did you know any other people around here at the time, like doing stuff like, playing piano? Yeah, anybody playing harp or anything like that?
Oh yeah, I'm sure I know this, Slim. How poor are you talking about it? His name, his records sound familiar, you know?
